surfaces.part: broken brick and mortar lump clusters

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64-wide, 48-row opaque rectangle (rows 0-47) of brown dust texture seen from above. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical south face. The brick and mortar lumps are small scattered clusters (about rows 2-15, 18-30 and 33-47) lying on the flat patch. Nothing stands up to give a front face, so this reads as a flat ground decal, which matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 5 visible tones per tile, between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, matching both references, so the soil has no large flat fills and carries a speckled grain with darker and lighter dust variation. The small brick clusters are edged with dark red-brown, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted by the adjacent material rather than a black sticker line. The brick lumps have about 3-4 tones each (highlight, face, shade, dark edge), slightly fewer steps than Beodeul's 5-6, and the debris is sparse and small. Overall it is a textured, tinted-outline ground patch that sits acceptably next to the grass reference.
